rows.why: The purpose of each customer-facing AI application, the public users it serves, what they expect from it and the settings it is deployed in are documented.
The application's knowledge limits, and how customers are told what its answers can and cannot be relied on for and when a human takes over, are documented.
The scope of what the customer-facing AI may answer or do, and the topics and data it must stay out of, is specified and documented.
The controls on the customer-facing application's components, such as input and output guardrails and separation of system instructions from user input, are identified and documented.
The likelihood and impact of public users attacking the application (prompt injection, abuse) and of wrong, harmful or leaked answers reaching customers, including their cost, are identified.
The customer-facing application's behaviour in production is monitored for abuse patterns, adversarial prompting and degraded or unsafe answers.
The accuracy and reliability of answers given to customers are tested before release and checked in use, with known limits recorded.
The application is evaluated for harmful or unsafe output to customers and shown to fail safely when it cannot answer.
The customer-facing application is security tested against prompt injection, jailbreaks, abuse and data extraction by public users, and its resilience is evaluated.
Customer interactions with the AI are logged with inputs, outputs and user attribution, so answers given to customers can be traced and accounted for.
The application is tested and monitored for answers that leak personal or confidential data to customers.
Answers given to different groups of customers are evaluated for bias and unfair treatment.
Customers can report wrong or harmful answers and appeal outcomes, and those reports feed the application's evaluation.
The residual risks the customer-facing application still poses to customers after controls are documented.

The risk treatments for the customer-facing application are applied and kept effective in operation: business rules that restrict what answers may go out, input and output guardrails, data loss checks on answers, and authentication and throttling of public users against abuse.
There are procedures to respond to and recover from new failures of the customer-facing AI, such as a successful injection or a leaked answer.
The customer-facing AI can be switched off or replaced by a fallback quickly when it behaves unsafely, and who may do so is known.
Incidents and errors in answers to customers are tracked, reviewed and communicated to affected customers and other relevant parties.

review.reason: The why covers only internal logging of interactions; for a customer-facing application the transparency risk is towards customers (being told they are dealing with AI, explanations of answers, recourse), which no row examines.
